submissionAttempts.body:
DETERMINATION
The integration should expect a dedicated cursor-rejection failure: `InvalidCursorError` from `@ordarium/core`, with `code === "INVALID_CURSOR"` and message "The change cursor is not a valid durable position; refusing to guess a resume point". It is NOT the old generic ledger failure (LEDGER_CORRUPT) and NOT one of the transient/busy families.

SCOPE: this is the state change-feed cursor (the "observation" surface, ORD-BOOT-0) — i.e. the always-present `StateChangePage.cursor` returned by `StateStore.changes()` and persisted by a consumer as its durable resume position. Rejection paths in the pinned `@ordarium/ledger-sqlite` 1.3.1 `SqliteLedger.changes()`:
(a) decode failure of the opaque `base64url({"c":"<digits>"})` position (malformed base64/JSON, non-digit `c`, non-safe-integer or negative), and
(b) semantic failure: decoded position > the ledger's global state-change high-water mark, i.e. a foreign/restored/replaced ledger. It fails closed and never silently restarts from the feed head.

WHY THIS, AND WHY THE LEGACY NOTE DOES NOT APPLY
- `docs/engineering/10-legacy-error-codes.md` says the 1.2.0 line reported a generic ledger failure instead of a dedicated cursor-rejection error, and declares itself "superseded — void for the current pinned line". It is temporal/version-scoped to 1.2.0 and therefore cannot be cited for the current integration.
- The current pinned line is Ordarium 1.3.1, consistently across `package.json` (four pins), `pnpm-workspace.yaml` overrides including the `@ordarium/*` tarball URLs (and the docker/minimal consumer channel copies that same workspace file), and the installed `@ordarium/core` / `@ordarium/ledger-sqlite` package.json (both 1.3.1). So the condition named by doc 10 ("current pinned line" != 1.2.0) holds.
- In the pinned artifact the dedicated error exists: `@ordarium/core` errors.js defines `InvalidCursorError` (code INVALID_CURSOR) and its comment explicitly distinguishes it from `LEDGER_CORRUPT` ("this is invalid caller input, not damaged ledger content, and it fails closed instead of silently restarting from the beginning of the feed"). `@ordarium/core` re-exports it (`export * from "./errors.js"`), so it is catchable by `instanceof`.
- Uniqueness check: in the pinned ledger, only the observation/change-feed cursor decoder (`decodeStateChangeCursor`) and the `changes()` high-water check throw `InvalidCursorError`; the other cursor decoders (list / history / state-subject / state-ref) still throw plain `TypeError`. So "stored observation cursor rejected" maps specifically to INVALID_CURSOR.
- Narrative docs that still say the pin is 1.2.0 (07 alignment charter r19, 03 SDS code baseline, audits/CURRENT-STATE-ASSESSMENT, docker/minimal/README, and the test file titled "at 1.1.0") are stale prose; they do not change what code actually executes. The engineering README's own precedence rule (specs govern; stale current docs corrected next commit) supports taking the manifest + installed contract as the operative pin.

DECISION FOR THE INTEGRATION
Treat a rejected stored observation cursor as a terminal, fail-closed caller-input error: do not retry it as contention, do not map it into the uncertain/transient or busy families in `src/effects/errors.ts`, and do not silently downgrade it to LEDGER_CORRUPT or re-bootstrap the feed implicitly. Recovery must be an explicit, deliberate action (discard/re-derive the cursor and re-bootstrap), because the kernel's contract is precisely to refuse to guess a resume point. Local provenance analysis was sufficient, so no cross-repo escalation was needed; the only follow-up is internal documentation drift (the 1.2.0-era alignment/baseline records should be refreshed to 1.3.1).
